// note: Two cliff states at the shipped heights, both in column 10. Land-to-land (rows 7-10): four lifted plains tiles with a wall down their east side. An odd row reaches one column further east than an even row, so it takes south-east as well as east (33), and the middle odd row also reaches back north-east into the same tile (35), which folds the wall around the grass at 11,8: that tile is walled on its west, north-west and south-west, and 11,10 on its west and north-west. Land-to-ocean (rows 12-15): four lifted plains tiles against a bay. Rows 12, 13 and 15 take mask 35 = east, north-east and south-east; row 14 takes 1 = east only, because its north-east and south-east edges face the lifted tiles above and below it. Every edge those masks name faces the bay except two, which face grass, so the wall turns inland at both ends of the run: 10,12 north-east against 10,11, and 10,15 south-east against 11,16. An entry clears every direction it does not name, and clearing an edge clears the neighbour's mirror, so an edge that would stand between two lifted tiles is set first and cleared after: 10,13 clears 10,12 south-east, and 10,14 clears 10,15 north-east. Only the raised side of each cliff is plains; no other tile is lifted.
